comparison: Both evaluations address the C45 domain mapping and D2018A mutant (C4-C7, C35-C38, C84, C86). OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED with converging experimental approaches. Peer reviewers also accepted this as SUPPORTED ('interesting finding', 'fine tool'), though requested extensions to TET2/TET3. Both agree the core mapping is solid.

Both address TPR deletion effects on TET1 binding (C34, C82-C83). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED but notes C82-C83 are speculative about mechanism (direct vs. structural). Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 1 finding it 'very strange' that all TPRs are important and questioning specificity. Both recognize interpretive limitations.

Both evaluate in vitro activity assays showing OGT stimulation of TET1 (C3, C8-C10, C39-C40, C85). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with good controls and quantitative data. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, noting the D2018A mutant 'still retained enzymatic activity' in cells, which 'contradicts major conclusions', and that modification vs. binding effects are unclear.

Both address zebrafish rescue experiments (C11-C15, C52). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with statistically significant results demonstrating functional importance in vivo. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, with concerns that D2018A may disrupt other interactions, lack of quantification/blinding, and unclear whether effects are direct or downstream.

Both evaluate mESC phenotypes including TET2 increase (C16-C17, C19, C44). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED, noting TET2 increase without transcript changes suggests post-transcriptional regulation. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, with editors requesting investigation of this 'complex' phenotype and noting the mechanism remained unexplained and potentially confounding.

Both address 5mC/5hmC phenotypes (C20-C21, C65). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED, explaining the paradox through increased TET2. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, finding the results 'complex and somewhat confusing' with inadequate explanation of reduced 5mC without increased 5hmC despite TET activity. OpenEval also covers C22-C24 which peer R6 addresses.

Both address 5hmC-Seal data showing few DhMRs (C22-C24). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED, noting consistency with redistribution rather than global loss. Peer review also rates SUPPORTED, accepting this as addressing editor concerns about genome-wide profiling, with few DhMRs consistent with unchanged total 5hmC.

Both evaluate WGBS data on DMR enrichment in gene bodies and correlation with DEGs (C28-C32). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED, noting the gene body enrichment is substantial and biologically interpretable. Peer review also rates SUPPORTED, accepting this analysis performed in response to editor requests for genome-wide profiling.

Both address methylation-expression correlations (C27, C68-C69). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED, noting weak promoter correlation but stronger gene body correlation. Peer review also rates SUPPORTED, accepting these correlation analyses though reviewers did not specifically comment. OpenEval notes the promoter correlation is statistically significant but biologically minimal.

Both address speculative interpretations about TET2 compensation (C66, C70-C71). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting the model is plausible but lacks direct validation. Peer review also rates UNCERTAIN, finding the compensatory TET2 explanation speculative and the paradox inadequately explained. Both recognize interpretive limitations.

Both evaluate the dual function model of OGT-TET1 interaction (C45-C51, C76-C77). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting the model integrates prior work but lacks direct evidence for chromatin recruitment. Peer review also rates UNCERTAIN, with reviewers noting the function 'remains somewhat speculative' and editors emphasizing mechanism needs substantive exploration.

Both address off-target CRISPR effects and control experiments (C87-C88). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED, noting appropriate controls demonstrate phenotypes are mutation-specific. Peer review also rates SUPPORTED, accepting this as a critical control for potential confounding, though added in revision so reviewers did not comment directly.

OpenEval rates C53 as UNCERTAIN because data are not shown, making evaluation impossible. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific claim about unpublished O-GlcNAc site identification.

OpenEval evaluates novelty claim C78 as UNCERTAIN, noting it appears accurate but cannot be fully verified. Peer review R1 includes C78 in their SUPPORTED evaluation of the C45 mapping, accepting it as 'an interesting finding' without specifically challenging the novelty claim.

OpenEval finds background/citation claims (C1-C2, C33, C54, C56-C58, C60-C63, C72-C74, C79-C81) SUPPORTED as accurately representing prior work. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers typically do not evaluate background citations.

OpenEval finds zebrafish model background (C41-C43) SUPPORTED as accurately cited. Peer review R3 includes these claims in their UNCERTAIN evaluation of the rescue experiments, but does not challenge the background model itself, only the interpretation of results using it.

OpenEval rates speculative extrapolations (C55, C59, C64, C75) as UNCERTAIN, noting they extend beyond experimental evidence. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these broader speculative claims about OGT regulating all TETs or nutrient-dependent regulation.
